text.content: A Cinder Vow Sworn is the Choir of Ash's field arm, not its contemplative wing — that role belongs to the Choir-sworn Vigil, whose whole discipline is patient faith banked slowly toward one enormous, campaign-defining act. The two paths share theology (Uriel's Turning as corruption-forced tragedy, not villainy) but split hard on doctrine of action. Where a Choir-sworn Vigil waits and prays for the day the Cage cracks on its own, a Cinder Vow Sworn does not wait: day to day, they escort relic-recovery teams into the Glasslands, hold ground against anyone trying to cap an unstable reactor the Choir has declared sacred, and stand sentinel over half-melted ghost-machine shrines they read as proof Uriel's will still moves in the world. Their operating belief is that small, controlled acts of destruction now are mercy that prevents a worse, uncontrolled Turning-repeat later — consistent with the Choir's core faith, but urgent where Vigil is patient. Not every Cinder Vow recruit holds the full theology sincerely; some are cynics bought with protection and power. Most, though, believe every word of it, which is what makes them dangerous to travel with.
